item.title: Leaf-peeping season is almost here: Where to see spectacular fall foliage across the US in 2026
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 6.20
Leaf-peeping season is almost here: Where to see spectacular fall foliage across the US in 2026 Editor's Note Autumn officially begins on Sept. 22, and that means leaf-peeping season will soon be here. Where and when the foliage will be most dramatic depends on location, altitude and weather. Leaves turn earlier in places with higher elevations and lower temperatures, so some parts of the northern and western U.S. are starting to see some color, while other destinations may not kick off their leaf-peeping seasons until October. If you'd like to plan a leaf-peeping trip this year, we've got you covered. Here are the best destinations you can visit over the coming weeks to see spectacular foliage. Related: Fall foliage cruises in New England, Canada and beyond When and where can we see fall foliage at its peak? Each fall, various forecast tools aim to predict the arrival of autumn foliage across the U.S. using precipitation and temperature statistics, historic trends for peak leaf peeping, local observations, and model outputs from previous years. Our favorites include The Old Farmer's Almanac and the Smoky Mountains Fall Foliage Prediction Map. Plus, camping app Hipcamp launched an interactive map to help you find campgrounds for leaf-peeping trips. Even with these tools, no one can guarantee exactly where and when foliage will peak — especially with unusual weather patterns on the rise. "Of course, past results do not necessarily indicate what will happen this year, but it should give you a fairly good idea of how fall leaves typically progress," an Old Farmer's Almanac representative said. Here, we'll cover the country's top destinations for leaf peeping, and when to visit each for your best chance at seeing spectacular fall colors. Best places in the US to see fall foliage Northeast For travelers on the East Coast, the foliage is just beginning to turn in New England's most popular leaf-peeping states. Prime destinations include the Vermont ski town of Stowe, the Berkshires mountain range in Massachusetts and Acadia National Park in Maine. You can expect mountainous regions to reach maximum color toward the end of September and early October. Lower-elevation areas, like the Hudson Valley in New York and Bar Harbor, Maine, may peak a little later. However, unexpected weather can shift these dates. Last year, a flash drought caused Vermont's leaves to drop early, while unseasonably warm weather in Pennsylvania delayed the leaf-peeping season. To stay updated on your destination, check local reports. Many states and regions offer fall foliage reports with predictions and regular updates throughout the season; Maine and the Poconos have already launched theirs for 2026. You can even sign up for local leaf-peeping newsletters to get updates in your inbox. Related: My first all-inclusive experience at a super-luxe upstate New York resort West The mountains of Colorado — known for their glorious gold and crimson aspen forests — are changing color earlier this year due to the state's prolonged drought. Peak foliage is expected to start in mid-September in the northern part of the state and travel south over the following weeks. The aptly named mountain town of Aspen is a great option, but there are plenty of brilliantly colored areas closer to Denver, such as Guanella Pass near Georgetown and Golden Gate Canyon State Park outside Golden. Utah's unearthly landscapes may be best known for their sandstone cliffs and gravity-defying arches, but they're also great places to enjoy the fall foliage of canyon maple, scrub oak and more come early to mid-October. Plus, the autumnal light illuminates the red rocks spectacularly. On the West Coast, Oregon's wild landscapes explode with color every fall. This year, Portland's foliage is expected to peak in mid- to late October. Take a steamboat ride to admire the changing leaves from the river, or drive the Columbia River Highway, a stretch of interstate designed specifically for its scenic vistas. Related: A points-fueled autumn road trip through Oregon's natural wonders Midwest Due to the Great Lakes' insulating effect, Michigan enjoys a long leaf-peeping season. This year's is already starting, with peak color forecast for early October in northern parts of the state and progressing south through late October. The famous M-119 road, also known as "Tunnel of Trees," recently reopened some sections after devastating floods earlier this year. Parts of Missouri, such as Lake of the Ozarks, are great candidates for a leaf-peeping trip as well. By Nov. 1, the maple, oak, hickory and ash trees along the lake's 1,150 miles of shoreline will be a riot of painterly hues. However, the American smoke tree, which turns an almost electric shade of pink, tends to peak much earlier. For a change of scenery, consider Lexington, Kentucky, where you can experience fall foliage from the water with a paddling tour along the Kentucky River or Elkhorn Creek. The leaves are expected to peak in the middle of November. Related: 5 stunning fall foliage road trips in the Midwest Mid-Atlantic and Southeast For endless views this fall, plan a road trip along the Blue Ridge Parkway or the North Carolina coast. The state boasts a long leaf-peeping season thanks to a wide range of elevations. You can see spectacular color in the Great Smoky Mountains on the state's western side starting in early October, and that peak will shift east over the coming weeks, hitting the coast in early November. Virginia's plentiful deciduous trees and varied landscape provide a long fall foliage season as well. The season should start in earnest toward the end of September, at which point the Virginia Department of Forestry will start updating its fall foliage report weekly. For thinner crowds, consider Columbia, South Carolina. This hidden gem will be packed with color in late October and early November, whether you stay in town to explore Riverbanks Zoo and Three Rivers Greenway or head to nearby Congaree National Park — home to some of the country's oldest and tallest deciduous trees. Related: The best national parks for a weekend getaway South The farther south you go, the later leaf-peeping season starts, giving you a few extra weeks to plan a trip. Plus, you may not have to contend with as many crowds in these colorful Southern destinations. For example, Louisiana has plenty of top spots for leaf peeping from late October through mid-November, including Chemin-A-Haut State Park, Lake Claiborne State Park and Jimmie Davis State Park. Experience the vibrant red leaves of the bigtooth maple trees in Lost Maples State Natural Area outside San Antonio. The leaves likely won't start to change until late October; check back here for updates. Or try Garner State Park in southern Texas, where you can explore 11 miles of hiking trails and take in the varied hues of cypress, oak, mesquite and persimmon trees. The town of Eureka Springs, Arkansas, is surrounded by enough blazing mountainsides to rival northern leaf-peeping spots — and it offers preserved Victorian buildings and therapeutic natural hot springs. Mid-October through early November is the best time to go. Related: Air Canada will return to San Antonio in 3-route expansion Bottom line If you're dreaming of a leaf-peeping trip, now is the time to book it. Even better, it doesn't have to eat up your travel budget or vacation days — with so many stellar destinations in the U.S., you can experience the magic of the season while staying close to home. Though tools like the ones we mentioned can't make any guarantees, they are useful guides for determining where and when to travel for optimal fall colors. This is especially true for the maps, which update based on real-world user data gathered as the season unfolds. But remember, any weather changes over the coming weeks could adjust the predicted peak timing for any of these places, so try to be as flexible as possible with your plans. We recommend booking changeable flights and hotel stays whenever possible. Related reading: TPG featured card | 4X | Earn 4X Membership Rewards® points per dollar spent on purchases at restaurants worldwide, on up to $50,000 in purchases per calendar year, then 1X points for the rest of the year. | | 4X | Earn 4X Membership Rewards® points per dollar spent at US supermarkets, on up to $25,000 in purchases per calendar year, then 1X points for the rest of the year. | | 5X | Earn 5X Membership Rewards® points on prepaid hotel stays booked through AmexTravel.com or the Amex Travel App™. | | 3X | Earn 3X Membership Rewards® points on flights booked through AmexTravel.com, the Amex Travel App™, or purchased directly from airlines. | | 2X | Earn 2X Membership Rewards® points on prepaid car rentals booked through AmexTravel.com or the Amex Travel App™ and cruises booked and paid through AmexTravel.com. | | 1X | Earn 1X Membership Rewards® point per dollar spent on all other eligible purchases. |

item.title: Chase Sapphire Reserve turns 10 with massive point giveaway, new credits and bigger DoorDash perk
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 5.82
Chase Sapphire Reserve turns 10 with massive point giveaway, new credits and bigger DoorDash perk The Chase Sapphire Reserve® (see rates and fees) is celebrating its 10th birthday — and it's doing so by handing out presents to cardholders. Those include a grand prize of a staggering 5.5 million Chase Ultimate Rewards points for one lucky cardholder, a bundle of limited-time travel offers and an increased monthly DoorDash credit that begins Oct. 1. Here's what Sapphire Reserve cardholders need to know about the increased DoorDash credit, new limited-time travel credits and the massive points giveaway. Increased monthly DoorDash credit on the Sapphire Reserve Currently, the Sapphire Reserve provides complimentary DoorDash DashPass* ($120 annual value), two $10 monthly DoorDash promos that can be used on grocery or retail DoorDash orders (but not traditional restaurant orders) and a $5 monthly DoorDash credit that can be used on eligible restaurant orders. Beginning Oct. 1, the Sapphire Reserve will increase the current $5 monthly credit to a $15 monthly credit that is eligible for use on all DoorDash orders, including restaurant orders. That will be offered in addition to the existing DoorDash-related benefits. That means eligible Sapphire Reserve DoorDash DashPass members can receive up to $35 in DoorDash value each month. *Must activate membership by Dec. 31, 2027 The more flexible $15 monthly DoorDash credit on the Sapphire Reserve is now quite similar to the up to $15 monthly (up to $35 in December) Uber Cash benefit on the American Express Platinum Card®, valid on Uber rides and Uber Eats orders in the U.S. (Note: Uber Cash will only be deposited into one Uber account when you add the Amex Platinum as a payment method and redeem with any Amex card.) Assuming you are as likely to use the increased credit as I am, this increases the value of the credits on this card by a full $120 a year, which is not insignificant. New one-time travel credits on the Sapphire Reserve In addition to the increased DoorDash credit, Chase is rolling out five limited-time travel offers to celebrate the Sapphire Reserve's 10th anniversary. Activation is required, and cardholders must complete payment by the applicable deadline to receive the offer. | Brand | Spending requirement | Offer | Deadline | |---|---|---|---| | IHG Hotels & Resorts stay | At least $500 | $125 credit back | Oct. 16 | | Miraval and Alila stay | At least $1,000 | $250 credit back | Dec. 14 | | JSX semiprivate flight | At least $200 | $200 credit back | Dec. 14 | | Sixt car rental | At least $500 | $125 credit back | Dec. 14 | | Wander vacation home rental | At least $1,500 | $350 credit back | Dec. 14 | The IHG offer applies to eligible U.S. stays, while the Miraval and Alila offer applies to eligible U.S. stays at participating World of Hyatt properties. You must have been a cardmember prior to Aug. 25, 2026 for the Sixt car rental offer. The terms also indicate that each of these requires payment directly with the retailer and isn't valid with bookings made via Chase Travel℠. That distinction is especially important with IHG. Sapphire Reserve cardholders already have access to a separate one-time $250 hotel statement credit through the end of 2026 for eligible prepaid hotel stays with select brands, including IHG, booked through Chase Travel. Since the new 10th-anniversary IHG offer requires booking directly with IHG, it appears you wouldn't be able to stack the two credits for the same stay under the terms. Related: Chase Sapphire Reserve statement credits: What they are and how to use them Enter to win up to 5.5 million Ultimate Rewards points Last but not least — especially if you win — is a contest that will award nine finalists 500,000 Chase points and one grand-prize winner 5.5 million Chase Ultimate Rewards points. To enter, cardmembers can post about their favorite trip since 2016 (the year the Sapphire Reserve launched) for a chance to recreate it with the Chase Sapphire Reserve. Ten finalists will advance to a public voting phase, with the grand-prize winner taking home 5.5 million points. Based on TPG's September 2026 valuations, 5.5 million Ultimate Rewards points would be worth an impressive $112,750, while 500,000 points would be worth a still-outstanding $10,250. The full contest rules and details can be found here. Bottom line The Sapphire Reserve was an absolute game changer when it sprang onto the rewards scene in 2016, and Chase is marking its 10th anniversary with several new ways for cardholders to get additional value. The limited-time travel offers could provide meaningful savings for cardholders who already have eligible purchases planned, while the winners of 500,000 to 5.5 million points are obviously sure to be thrilled. But the expansion of the DoorDash credit is especially good news, as that perk will stick around even after the card's birthday candles are blown out. To learn more, read our full review of the Chase Sapphire Reserve. Apply here: Chase Sapphire Reserve

item.title: Wyndham Rewards guide: How to earn and redeem points, elite status and more
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 5.74
Wyndham Rewards guide: How to earn and redeem points, elite status and more Wyndham Rewards is one of the lesser-known hotel loyalty programs, especially when compared to major players like Marriott Bonvoy and Hilton Honors. But Wyndham Rewards has been making some major changes in 2026, including refreshing its cobranded cards and launching a premium card in June and switching to a four-tier award chart on Sept. 15. Plus, Chase Ultimate Rewards added Wyndham as a transfer partner in February, and Wells Fargo Rewards added it in April. With all these changes, here's what you need to know about the Wyndham Rewards loyalty program. What is Wyndham Rewards? Wyndham Rewards is the loyalty program for Wyndham Hotels & Resorts, which has around 8,400 hotels across 25 brands in about 100 countries. Wyndham includes budget-friendly brands like Howard Johnson, Super 8, Days Inn and Travelodge, as well as higher-end brands like Wyndham Grand, Esplendor Boutique Hotels and Registry Collection Hotels. But, despite the name, Echo Suites Extended Stay by Wyndham hotels don't participate in Wyndham Rewards. Although it has a sizable worldwide footprint, Wyndham Rewards doesn't offer as many elite benefits as other programs. However, earning Wyndham points is easy, and the program maintains a four-tier award chart. Many of the ways to earn and redeem Wyndham Rewards points vary by country of residence. For simplicity, this guide assumes you reside in the U.S. Also, for simplicity, this guide discusses cardholder benefits for accounts opened on or after June 17; if you opened your Wyndham card earlier, your benefits may differ. Wyndham Rewards elite status Wyndham Rewards offers four standard member tiers, plus an invite-only Titanium status that's primarily for hotel owners. You'll progress to higher standard elite tiers as you complete qualifying nights at Wyndham Hotels & Resorts properties each calendar year. | | Annual requirements | Incremental perks | Cards and subscriptions that offer this status as a perk | |---|---|---|---| | Blue | None | Free Wi-Fi and rollover elite nights | None | | Gold | Five nights | Preferred room choice, 10% bonus points on stays and late checkout | | | Platinum | 15 nights | Early check-in and 15% bonus points on stays | | | Diamond | 40 nights | Suite upgrades, a welcome amenity and 20% bonus points on stays | | The information for the Wyndham Rewards Earner Card, the Wyndham Rewards Debit Card, the Wyndham Rewards Earner Plus Card, the Wyndham Rewards Earner Premier Card and the Wyndham Rewards Earner Business Card has been collected independently by The Points Guy. The card details on this page have not been reviewed or provided by the card issuer. Once you earn Wyndham status through qualifying nights, you'll keep it through the end of the calendar year after you earned it. You'll usually need to book directly with Wyndham to get elite earnings and benefits. However, some stays booked through independent travel agents can qualify if booked at loyalty-eligible rates. Wyndham Blue status All Wyndham Rewards members start at the Blue membership tier, and there aren't any requirements you must meet to maintain this tier. Blue members can get free Wi-Fi, earn points on stays, roll over qualifying nights to the next calendar year and access member rates. Wyndham Gold status Wyndham Rewards members earn Gold status after completing five qualifying nights in a calendar year. Additionally, cardholders of the Wyndham Rewards Earner Card and the Wyndham Rewards Debit Card get Wyndham Gold status automatically, as do Wyndham Rewards Insider members. In addition to the perks offered to Blue members, Gold members get their preferred room choice within the category they've booked, 10% bonus points on stays and late checkout up to two hours past the standard checkout time (upon request and subject to availability). Wyndham Platinum status Earning Wyndham Platinum status requires just 15 qualifying nights per calendar year. Additionally, cardholders of the Wyndham Rewards Earner Plus Card receive Wyndham Platinum status as a cardholder perk after their first year (but Diamond status for their first year). In addition to the perks offered to Gold members, Platinum members receive a 15% bonus on points for stays and early check-in up to two hours before the standard check-in time (upon request and subject to availability). Platinum members can also enjoy rental car upgrades through Alamo, National and Enterprise at participating locations in the U.S. and Canada, and status match to Caesars Rewards each year (only if your Wyndham status is earned through stays). Wyndham Diamond status After staying 40 nights per calendar year, Wyndham members earn Diamond elite status. Additionally, cardholders of the Wyndham Rewards Earner Premier Card and the Wyndham Rewards Earner Business Card get Wyndham Diamond status automatically. Plus, cardholders of the Wyndham Rewards Earner Plus Card receive Diamond status for their first year. In addition to the perks offered to Platinum members, Wyndham Diamond members get 20% bonus points on stays, suite upgrades (upon request and subject to availability), a complimentary snack or beverage when staying at select hotel brands and the ability to give Gold status to a family member or friend once per calendar year (only if you earn your Wyndham status through stays). Wyndham Rewards Insider subscription You can buy an annual Wyndham Rewards Insider subscription for $95 per year. In return, the perks of the subscription include: - At least 10% off the standard rate at Hotels by Wyndham when you book directly - Wyndham Gold status - Discounts on travel bundle bookings - Discounted cruise rates and theme park tickets - A one-time 7,500-point welcome bonus Status match to Wyndham You can match select elite status tiers with other hotel loyalty programs to Wyndham Rewards once per calendar year. Specifically, here's which hotel elite status tiers match which Wyndham Rewards tiers: | | Match to Wyndham Gold | Match to Wyndham Platinum | Match to Wyndham Diamond | |---|---|---|---| | Best Western Rewards | Blue | Gold, Platinum and Diamond | Diamond Select | | Choice Privileges | Member | Gold and Platinum | Diamond | | Hilton Honors | Member | Silver | Gold and higher | | IHG One Rewards | Member | Silver Elite and Gold Elite | Platinum Elite and higher | | Marriott Bonvoy | Member | Silver Elite | Gold Elite and higher | | Omni Select Guest | Insider | Champion | Ikon | | Radisson Rewards | Club | Premium | VIP | | World of Hyatt | Member | Discoverist and Explorist | Globalist | To request a status match, go to this page, sign into your Wyndham Rewards account and complete the status match request form (including submitting proof of your elite status in another program). Then you should be awarded Wyndham status within five to seven days of submitting the form. Once you have the matched status, you'll keep the status for 90 days. But if you complete a specific number of qualifying nights within 90 days, you'll keep the status through Dec. 31 of the next calendar year. Specifically, if you matched to Gold, one qualifying night within 90 days will let you keep Gold through the end of the next calendar year. Likewise, four qualifying nights will let you keep a matched Platinum status, and 10 qualifying nights will let you keep a matched Diamond status. Related: Complete guide to current hotel elite status match and challenge offers Is Wyndham status worth it? Wyndham Rewards elite status can be useful, but it's usually not worth striving to earn it through hotel stays. Even Diamond status, which requires 40 qualifying nights per calendar year, only provides a 20% bonus on points earned from stays, along with perks like space-available suite upgrades and a welcome amenity. By comparison, Hilton Honors Silver members get a 20% points bonus after just 10 nights, while World of Hyatt Explorist members get a 20% bonus after 30 nights. Marriott Bonvoy members earn Gold Elite status after 25 nights and receive a 25% points bonus. Higher tiers with Hilton, Marriott and Hyatt also tend to offer more valuable on-property perks, such as breakfast or lounge access. That said, Wyndham status is relatively easy to get without staying dozens of nights. Several Wyndham cards provide elite status as a perk, and Wyndham also offers a status match from many competing hotel loyalty programs. So, while you likely shouldn't book stays just to earn Wyndham status, it's certainly worth using the benefits if you can get status through a card, status match or stays you'd complete anyway. How to earn Wyndham points There are a few different ways you can earn Wyndham points. Here's an overview of your options. Earn Wyndham points on stays On qualifying stays, Wyndham Rewards members earn as follows: - 10 points per dollar of room rate paid to the participating property: AmericInn, Baymont, Days Inn, Dazzler, Esplendor, Hawthorn Extended Stay, Howard Johnson, La Quinta, Microtel, Ramada, Registry Collection, Super 8, Trademark Collection, Travelodge, TRYP by Wyndham, Vienna House by Wyndham, Wingate by Wyndham, Wyndham Alltra, participating Caesars Rewards properties and participating destinations - 10 points per dollar of total folio paid to the participating hotel: Applicable Dolce Hotels and Resorts, Wyndham Grand, Wyndham Hotels and Resorts (including Viva Wyndham properties) and Wyndham Garden properties - 5 points per dollar of room rate paid to the participating hotel: WaterWalk Extended Stay by Wyndham (only qualified stays in furnished suites) When staying at most Wyndham Hotels & Resorts or participating vacation club resorts, your earnings are rounded up to 1,000 points per qualifying stay if you would otherwise have earned less based on your room rate or total folio. You can earn points for up to three rooms or condos per night by associating your member number with each one. Gold, Platinum and Diamond members earn a percentage bonus on their base earnings from qualifying Wyndham stays. Specifically, Gold members get a 10% bonus, Platinum members get a 15% bonus and Diamond members get a 20% bonus. Wyndham Rewards also occasionally offers promotions that let you earn bonus points on stays. So keep an eye out for Wyndham promotions and register even if you aren't sure you'll have any qualifying stays during the promotion period. Finally, remember that bookings through third-party online travel agencies usually aren't qualifying. So, book your Wyndham stays on the Wyndham website or app to ensure you'll earn points and enjoy elite status benefits. Related: How I earned 24,500 points from $180 in hotel stays Earn points with cobranded Wyndham cards Wyndham Rewards offers several cobranded credit cards and a cobranded debit card. To earn Wyndham points on everyday purchases, review the Wyndham cards and determine which best fits your spending habits. - Wyndham Rewards Debit Card: 1 point per dollar spent on eligible purchases made at participating Hotels by Wyndham and qualifying gas and grocery purchases, and 1 point per $2 spent on all other qualifying purchases (earnings capped at 7,500 bonus points each anniversary year) - Wyndham Rewards Earner Card: 5 points per dollar spent on eligible purchases made at Hotels by Wyndham (including hotels through Wyndham travel bundles); 3 points per dollar spent on eligible vacation club, dining and grocery store purchases (excluding Target and Walmart), as well as eligible gas and electric vehicle charging purchases; and 1 point per dollar spent on all other purchases (excluding Vacation Club down payments) - Wyndham Rewards Earner Plus Card: 6 points per dollar spent on eligible purchases made at Hotels by Wyndham (including hotels through Wyndham travel bundles); 4 points per dollar spent on eligible vacation club, travel, dining and grocery store purchases (excluding Target and Walmart); and 1 point per dollar spent on all other purchases (excluding vacation club down payments) - Wyndham Rewards Earner Premier Card: 8 points per dollar spent on eligible purchases made at Hotels by Wyndham (including hotels through Wyndham travel bundles); 4 points per dollar spent on eligible vacation club, travel, dining and grocery store purchases (excluding Target and Walmart); and 1 point per dollar spent on all other purchases (excluding vacation club down payments) - Wyndham Rewards Earner Business Card: 8 points per dollar spent on eligible purchases made at Hotels by Wyndham (including Wyndham travel bundles); 5 points per dollar spent on eligible vacation club, gas, EV charging, marketing, advertising, office supply store and shipping purchases; and 1 point per dollar spent on all other purchases (excluding vacation club down payments) These cards are great for earning Wyndham points, especially if you spend a lot at participating Hotels by Wyndham or on Wyndham travel bundles. Plus, some of these cards give cardholders bonus points each anniversary year after payment of the annual fee. These bonus points could get you a few free nights and can partially — and, in some cases, fully — offset the card's annual fee. | Card | Annual fee | Anniversary bonus points | Value of bonus points based on TPG's September 2026 valuation | |---|---|---|---| | Wyndham Rewards Earner Plus Card | $95 | 15,000 | $105 | | Wyndham Rewards Earner Premier Card | $395 | 30,000 | $210 | | Wyndham Rewards Earner Business Card | $149 | 15,000 | $105 | Related: Which of the 4 Wyndham Rewards credit cards is right for you? Transfer rewards to Wyndham You can transfer several types of transferable rewards currencies to Wyndham Rewards at the following ratios: - Bilt: 1:1 - Capital One miles: 1:1 - Chase Ultimate Rewards: 1:1 - Citi ThankYou Rewards: 1:1 for ThankYou cards with annual fees and 1:0.7 for ThankYou cards with no annual fee - Wells Fargo Rewards: 1:2 The most favorable transfer ratio is offered by Wells Fargo Rewards. But in each case, other transfer partners may give you more value for your rewards. Other ways to earn Wyndham points - Book Wyndham Rewards travel bundles: When you book your hotel, flights, car rental and activities through Wyndham Rewards, you can earn up to 10 points per dollar spent on qualifying hotel stays and activities and 1 point per dollar spent on all other travel reservations. - Buy Wyndham points: You can buy up to 100,000 points per calendar year for your account. Standard points pricing is 1.3 cents each, but you'll sometimes see points on sale for as much as a 100% bonus, which brings the purchase cost down to 0.65 cents per point. - Dine Out with Wyndham Rewards: You can earn up to 5 Wyndham points per dollar spent on dine-in and takeout orders when you use a card you've linked to the Dine Out with Wyndham Rewards program to pay at a participating restaurant. - Host a meeting or event: Planners earn 1 point per dollar spent on qualifying group, meeting and event spending, including rooms when you book 10 or more rooms on at least one night of your event, event space cost and event food-and-beverage charges. However, note that not all properties participate in the Groups, Meetings & Events program. - Book rental cars: Earn 2 Wyndham points per dollar spent and enjoy discounted rates when you book an Alamo, Enterprise or National rental car at a qualifying rate through the Wyndham Hotels & Resorts website. Note that you won't earn rental car rewards on your rental. - Take surveys: You can earn Wyndham points by taking surveys through the Opinion Rewards Panel or e-Rewards. - Buy through Ticketmaster: If you link your Wyndham Rewards account to your Ticketmaster account, you'll earn 1 Wyndham point per dollar spent on the base ticket price for eligible purchases made on the official Ticketmaster website while logged into your Ticketmaster account (up to a maximum of 25,000 Wyndham Rewards points per calendar year; Wyndham Rewards Insider members earn 2 points per dollar spent). How to redeem Wyndham Rewards points There are several ways to redeem Wyndham Rewards points. TPG's September 2026 valuations have Wyndham Rewards points at 0.7 cents each, so you'll typically want to get at least 0.7 cents per Wyndham point on redemptions. Redeem for free nights The best way to use your Wyndham Rewards points is usually for award nights at participating hotels, participating Caesars Rewards properties, participating destinations and Cottages.com properties. As of Sept. 15, Wyndham has an award chart with four different pricing tiers: 5,000, 15,000, 30,000 and 45,000 points per night. You'll find 1,788 Wyndham hotels and resorts at the 5,000-point tier. Many of these properties belong to budget-friendly brands and can be found along major expressways or in off-the-beaten-path destinations. However, nine Club Wyndham vacation properties can be booked for just 5,000 points per night, including the Club Wyndham Cypress Palms in Florida and the Club Wyndham Legacy Golf Resort in Arizona. You'll also find some full-service properties in this tier, including the Palma Resort Phu Quoc, Trademark Collection by Wyndham in Vietnam and the Wyndham Corfu Acharavi in Greece. At the 15,000-point tier, you'll find 3,665 properties. Some of our favorite sweet spots at the 15,000-point tier are the Grand Decameron Panama, A Trademark All Inclusive Resort in Panama; the Viva Heavens by Wyndham, A Trademark All Inclusive in the Dominican Republic; the Wyndham Grand Athens in Greece; and the WorldMark Steamboat Springs in Colorado. Moving on to the 30,000-point tier, you'll find 2,882 properties. These properties are usually upscale hotels, but some are simply properties in appealing destinations. Some of our favorites include the Kunuku Resort All Inclusive Curacao, Trademark by Wyndham; the Club Wyndham Midtown 45 in New York City; and the Margaritaville Vacation Club — St. Thomas in the U.S. Virgin Islands. And 68 properties are at the 45,000-point tier. These properties include the Wyndham Grand Clearwater Beach in Florida, the Esplendor by Wyndham Isla Mujeres Boutique All Inclusive in Mexico and the Wyndham Alltra Punta Cana All Inclusive Resort in the Dominican Republic. Interestingly, you can book multibedroom accommodations at nine Wyndham Vacation Club properties for just 5,000 points per bedroom, per night. As such, a two-bedroom villa at select Wyndham Vacation Club properties could cost just 10,000 points per night. You can also book Cottages.com properties in the U.K. for 15,000 points per bedroom, per night, though you'll need to call to book. When booking free night awards with their account, select Wyndham cardholders get a redemption discount: - 10% redemption discount: Wyndham Rewards Earner Card and Wyndham Rewards Earner Plus Card - 20% redemption discount: Wyndham Rewards Earner Business Card - 25% redemption discount: Wyndham Rewards Earner Premier Card You'll need the full standard amount of points in your account to book an award via the Wyndham website or app, even if you have access to a redemption discount. However, cardholders can call to book an award stay if they don't have enough points to cover the standard award cost but do have enough for the discounted award cost. Finally, you can also book Points + Cash nights for stays at participating hotels, participating Caesars Rewards properties and participating destinations. Specifically, here's how the award costs break down for Points + Cash stays: - 5,000-point property: Starting at 500 points plus cash - 15,000-point property: Starting at 1,500 points plus cash - 30,000-point property: Starting at 3,000 points plus cash - 45,000-point property: Starting at 4,500 points plus cash Redeem for Wyndham Rewards Experiences You can bid and redeem Wyndham points for experiences via the Wyndham Rewards Experiences platform. The options change frequently but often include VIP tickets to performances and sporting events. They also occasionally include special meet-and-greets with celebrities. Related: 8 of the most exclusive travel experiences you can book with points and miles Other ways to redeem Wyndham points - Partner travel currency: You can redeem Wyndham points for points or miles with select travel partners, including United MileagePlus, Air Canada Aeroplan and Avianca Lifemiles. Doing so will usually provide poor value compared to award nights, though. - AARP membership: You can redeem 3,000 Wyndham points to join AARP or renew your membership for one year. This typically costs $20 per year, so you'll get 0.67 cents per point. - Retail gift cards: You can redeem Wyndham points for gift cards. Most types of retail gift cards cost 3,000 points for a $10 card, 7,500 points for a $25 card, 14,000 points for a $50 card and 27,000 points for a $100 card. This means you'd get between 0.33 and 0.37 cents per point when redeeming for most gift cards. - Visa gift cards: If you prefer to cash out your Wyndham points, you can redeem them for Visa prepaid cards. The cards expire after six months and cost 8,000 points for a $25 card, 15,000 points for a $50 card and 29,000 points for a $100 card. This means you'd get between 0.31 and 0.34 cents per point. - Points Payback: Eligible Wyndham cardholders can redeem points for statement credits toward purchases made within the previous 90 days. - Merchandise: You can redeem Wyndham points for a wide range of merchandise. For example, Bose QuietComfort Earbud Headphones would cost 61,122 Wyndham points. With a comparable paid rate of $149 through Amazon, you'd get 0.24 cents per point. - Charitable donations: You can donate as few as 500 Wyndham points to a selection of charities. - Airline tickets, car rentals and private transportation: You can also redeem Wyndham points to book airline tickets, rental cars and private transportation. Most redemption options in this section offer well under TPG's valuation of Wyndham points, as you'll usually get much better value when you use your Wyndham points for award nights. Do Wyndham Rewards points expire? Wyndham Rewards points generally expire four years after they're posted to your account. However, your points could expire sooner if 18 consecutive months pass without any earning, redeeming or transferring activity for your Wyndham points. One exception to the standard Wyndham points expiration rules is that points earned by a Wyndham Rewards Earner Premier Card member won't expire as long as the card account is open and in good standing. However, if you close your card or your account is no longer considered in good standing, your points will become subject to the standard expiration rules again. Related: How to keep your points and miles from expiring Wyndham Rewards pros and cons If you're considering whether to use the Wyndham Rewards program, here's a summary of the pros: - Simple fixed award chart with four redemption tiers - Large footprint of around 8,400 hotels in about 100 countries - Relatively easy to earn points, including a minimum of 1,000 points on most qualifying stays - Multiple transferable rewards partners, including Bilt, Capital One, Chase, Citi and Wells Fargo - Elite status is easy to get through Wyndham cards and status matches - Eligible Wyndham cardholders get a 10% to 25% discount on free night awards But the program isn't perfect. Here's a summary of the cons: - Elite benefits are weak compared with major competitors like Hilton, Marriott and Hyatt. - Even Diamond status doesn't include perks like complimentary breakfast and lounge access. - Many nonhotel redemptions offer significantly less value than award stays. - Points usually expire after four years, or sooner if your account is inactive for 18 months. Wyndham Rewards won't be the best fit for every traveler. But its fixed award chart, broad hotel footprint, multiple transfer partners and accessible elite status can still make the program useful, particularly when cash rates are high or you find a compelling redemption opportunity. Frequently asked questions Wyndham Rewards is free to join, and even entry-level members get benefits like free Wi-Fi and access to member rates. Wyndham Rewards points generally expire four years after they are posted to your account. However, you could lose your points sooner if you go 18 consecutive months without earning, redeeming or transferring points. TPG values Wyndham Rewards points at 0.7 cents each as of September 2026. However, you may get significantly more or less value depending on how you redeem your points. As of Sept. 15, 2026, Wyndham Rewards free nights cost 5,000, 15,000, 30,000 or 45,000 points per bedroom per night. Some eligible Wyndham cardholders get a 10% to 25% discount when redeeming points for free nights. Wyndham Rewards free nights and Points + Cash nights both count as qualifying nights toward elite status. However, if you book multiple rooms or units for the same night, only the one you stay in counts as a qualifying night. U.S. travelers can transfer Bilt Points, Capital One miles, Chase Ultimate Rewards points, Citi ThankYou Rewards points and Wells Fargo Rewards points to Wyndham Rewards. Transfer ratios vary by program, though, and transferring to Wyndham won't always provide the best value for your transferable rewards.

item.title: How to earn Choice Privileges points
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 4.95
How to earn Choice Privileges points Editor's Note Choice Privileges points have fueled many memorable stays for me over the years. For example, I once spent almost a month at an all-inclusive resort using Choice points. I've redeemed Choice points to stay near U.S. ski resorts. And I've also used Choice points to book numerous modestly priced award nights for city center stays in Japan and Europe. While award prices in the Choice Privileges program have crept up over the last few years and you'll no longer find widespread 8,000-point award nights in Japan, it's still possible to get significant value when redeeming Choice points for stays. Sports fans and concert lovers can also find good value when redeeming Choice points for experiences. But you need to earn Choice points before you can redeem them. So, here are some of the ways you can earn Choice points. Earn Choice points with hotel stays I'll start with the most obvious way to earn Choice points: staying at Choice hotels. You'll earn 10 Choice Privileges points per dollar spent on most points-eligible stays at Cambria, Clarion, Clarion Pointe, Comfort, Econo Lodge, Quality, Rodeway Inn, Sleep Inn and Ascend Collection properties in the following regions: - The United States - Canada - Europe (excluding Denmark, Estonia, Finland, Iceland, Latvia, Lithuania, Norway and Sweden) - The Middle East - Mexico - Brazil - Ecuador - Colombia - Guyana - Central America - The Caribbean - The Asia-Pacific region (including China, Japan, Thailand, Malaysia and India) This includes qualifying stays at participating Bluegreen Vacations resorts and Penn Entertainment casino hotels when you book through Choice. You'll earn points based on how long you stay at Everhome Suites, MainStay Suites and Suburban Studios properties. If you stay six nights or less, you'll earn 10 points per dollar spent. However, if you stay seven nights or longer, you'll earn 5 points per dollar spent on the first 30 nights and no points for additional nights after the first 30. You'll also earn 10 Choice points per dollar when staying at Radisson Individuals, Radisson Collection, Radisson Blu, Radisson, Radisson Red, Park Plaza, Park Inn by Radisson and Country Inn & Suites by Radisson properties in the following regions: - The United States - Canada - Latin America - The Caribbean You usually won't earn points on taxes and incidental charges. However, you'll earn points on food-and-beverage purchases made at participating Radisson Individuals, Radisson Collection, Radisson Blu, Radisson, Radisson Red and Park Plaza properties in the Americas when you charge the food and beverages to your room's folio. You won't earn points on stays at WoodSpring Suites properties or at Radisson properties outside of the above regions. Additionally, you'll only earn points on points-eligible stays that are booked directly with a hotel or through Choice's reservation line, website or mobile app. However, the following types of stays aren't points-eligible: - Rooms booked using an ineligible rate plan or for less than $40 per night - Some hotel-initiated promotions - Reward night stays - Complimentary rooms - Points plus cash reservations - Rooms paid for as part of a convention or meeting - Rooms booked through a travel agent or third-party online retailer, including online travel agencies (unless otherwise expressly noted), wholesale packages and group tours - Stays booked using the employee discount or the friends-and-family discount You can earn points on up to four rooms per night at the same hotel, though you will only receive bonus points for one room per stay. All the rooms must be in your name, you must pay in full for them and you must stay in one of them. Elite bonuses Except as noted above, Choice Privileges members earn 10 points per dollar spent on eligible stays. Members with Choice elite status also get bonus points based on their status tier: - Gold: 10% bonus - Platinum: 25% bonus - Diamond and Titanium: 50% bonus Gold, Platinum, Diamond and Titanium elite members also get a welcome gift on points-earning stays at select properties. However, this welcome gift varies based on brand and location as follows: - Ascend Collection and Comfort: 250 points or a complimentary snack and beverage - Cambria Hotels, Country Inn & Suites by Radisson, Park Inn by Radisson, Park Plaza, Radisson, Radisson Blu, Radisson Individuals and Radisson Red: 250 points - Clarion, Clarion Pointe, MainStay Suites, Quality, Sleep Inn and Suburban Studios: 200 points or a complimentary snack and beverage - Econo Lodge and Rodeway Inn: 100 points or a complimentary snack and beverage - Everhome Suites: 200 points Based on TPG's September 2026 valuations, 100 to 250 Choice points are only worth 85 cents to $2.12, so don't feel bad about indulging if you'd value a snack and drink higher than the points. Related: How TPG determines its points and miles valuations Return-and-earn bonus Each calendar year, Choice Privileges members earn 1,000 bonus points after completing two separate points-eligible stays. You'll earn another 1,000 bonus points after completing a third points-eligible stay in the same calendar year. Milestone rewards You can earn points or gift cards as milestone rewards each calendar year when you accrue milestone qualifying nights or milestone qualifying credits. | Milestone | Points option | Gift card option (only for U.S. and Canada residents) | |---|---|---| | 10 milestone qualifying nights or 20,000 milestone qualifying credits | 1,500 | $5 | | 20 milestone qualifying nights or 40,000 milestone qualifying credits | 2,500 | $10 | | 25 milestone qualifying nights or 50,000 milestone qualifying credits | 3,000 | $10 | | 30 milestone qualifying nights or 60,000 milestone qualifying credits | 3,500 | $10 | | 40 milestone qualifying nights or 80,000 milestone qualifying credits | 4,500 | $20 | | 45 milestone qualifying nights or 90,000 milestone qualifying credits | 5,000 | $20 | | 50 milestone qualifying nights or 100,000 milestone qualifying credits | 6,500 | $20 | Milestone qualifying nights include points-eligible nights, reward nights and nights booked under employee or friends-and-family rates at participating Choice Hotels properties. Meanwhile, you'll generally earn 10 milestone qualifying credits per dollar spent on qualifying stays, excluding taxes and incidental charges. U.S. members with a linked Choice Privileges credit card can also earn milestone qualifying credits equal to the points earned on qualifying card purchases. However, for extended-stay brands on stays of seven nights or longer, you'll earn milestone qualifying credits at the same rate as points and just one milestone qualifying night for every two nights, capped at 15 per stay. Bonus points packages When booking a stay at the flexible rate, you can often select a 1,000-, 2,000- or 5,000-point accelerator package. These packages provide the specified points each night in addition to the points you'd typically earn. In this case, you'd pay an additional $24.46 per night for the 1,000-point package, $30.89 per night for the 2,000-point package and $50.20 per night for the 5,000-point package. That means at best you'd be paying just over 1 cent per point. Choice Privileges credit cards You can earn Choice points with the two cobranded Choice Privileges credit cards. The Choice Privileges® Select Mastercard® offers: - 10 points per dollar spent on stays at participating Choice Hotels properties - 5 points per dollar spent on phone plan services and purchases at gas stations, grocery stores and home improvement stores - 1 point per dollar spent on other purchases The card carries a $95 annual fee but offers 30,000 bonus points every account anniversary and 20 elite night credits each calendar year. See our Choice Privileges Select Mastercard review for more details. The information for the Choice Privileges Select Mastercard has been collected independently by The Points Guy. The card details on this page have not been reviewed or provided by the card issuer. If you prefer a no-annual-fee card, the Choice Privileges® Mastercard® is also an option. This card earns: - 5 points per dollar spent on stays at participating Choice Hotels properties - 3 points per dollar spent on phone plan services and purchases at gas stations, grocery stores and home improvement stores - 1 point per dollar spent on other purchases Cardholders also get 10 elite night credits each calendar year, enough for Gold status. See our Choice Privileges Mastercard review for more details. The information for the Choice Privileges Mastercard has been collected independently by The Points Guy. The card details on this page have not been reviewed or provided by the card issuer. Related: The best hotel credit cards with annual fees under $100 Transfer rewards to Choice Another way to earn Choice points is to transfer rewards to the program. Specifically, you can transfer: - Wells Fargo Rewards points to Choice points at a 1:2 ratio - Citi ThankYou Rewards points to Choice points at a 1:1.5 ratio for premium cards and a 1:1.05 ratio for no-annual-fee cards - American Express Membership Rewards points to Choice points at a 1:1 ratio - Capital One miles to Choice points at a 1:1 ratio However, note that each program may only allow transfers in specific increments. It's also worth considering whether converting transferable rewards to Choice points is the best value way to use your transferable rewards. Buy Choice points You can also buy Choice points. Normally, you can buy up to 4,000 Choice points for 1.28 cents each, 5,000 to 9,000 Choice points for 1.14 cents each and 10,000 or more Choice points for 1.03 cents each. You can purchase or receive as a gift up to 180,000 Choice points each calendar year. Choice frequently offers promotions that let you buy points at a lower rate, so it's worth checking for an offer before purchasing points. Related: Buying points and miles saved me over $1,000 on flights and a hotel stay Other ways to earn Choice points Here are several other ways you can earn Choice points. Take surveys You can earn Choice points by taking surveys through the e-Rewards Opinion Panel. You'll earn 500 bonus points when you take your first survey, and then you'll earn additional points for every subsequent survey you take. Go on a cruise There are many ways to get a good deal on a cruise. But if earning Choice points is important, you may want to book your next cruise through Choice Privileges Cruises. By doing so, you'll earn 5 Choice points per dollar spent when you provide your Choice Privileges member number at the time of booking. Rent from Avis or Budget You can earn Choice points on Avis and Budget rental cars when you use the Choice Privileges Avis worldwide discount number (O418900) or the Choice Privileges Budget customer discount number (T134900) and provide your Choice Privileges number when renting. You'll usually earn 1,000 Choice points per rental, but promotions occasionally let you earn more. Plan a meeting You can use the Planner Rewards program to earn points when hosting a qualifying event at participating Cambria Hotels properties and Radisson brands in the U.S., Canada, Latin America and the Caribbean. You'll earn 3 points per dollar spent on eligible charges, including meeting space, guest rooms, food and beverages. There's no minimum spending requirement, but you can only earn up to 150,000 points per event at Cambria Hotels, and you'll need to book at least 10 sleeping rooms on at least one night of your event at Cambria Hotels. Bottom line I have gotten significant value from Choice Privileges points over the years, especially for award stays in Japan and Europe. So, even though Choice points aren't the most valuable hotel currency on paper, they're still a balance I like having available. Staying at Choice hotels is the most obvious way to earn Choice points, but credit card spending, transferable rewards and several partners can also help you build your balance. Just consider how you plan to redeem your Choice points before transferring rewards or buying points. Frequently asked questions The most straightforward way to earn Choice Privileges points is through eligible stays at participating Choice Hotels properties. You can also earn points with Choice credit cards, transfer points from several transferable rewards programs, buy Choice points and earn through select partners. Choice Privileges members generally earn 10 points per dollar spent on eligible stays at participating hotels. However, earning rates vary for some extended-stay properties, and elite members can earn a 10% to 50% bonus depending on their status tier. Choice Privileges reward nights aren't eligible for points, so you won't earn Choice Privileges points on the room rate. However, reward nights can count as milestone qualifying nights toward Choice Privileges milestone rewards. You can transfer rewards to Choice Privileges from Wells Fargo Rewards, Citi ThankYou Rewards, American Express Membership Rewards and Capital One. Transfer ratios vary by program, so consider the value of the rewards you're transferring before moving them to Choice. You can earn Choice points through Choice credit cards and partners such as Choice Privileges Cruises, Avis, Budget and e-Rewards. You can also earn points on qualifying stays at participating Bluegreen Vacations resorts and Penn Entertainment casino hotels, transfer eligible credit card rewards to Choice or buy Choice points.

item.title: Chase doubles The Edit hotel credit on Sapphire Reserve for Business to $1,000, adds earning cap
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 4.87
Chase doubles The Edit hotel credit on Sapphire Reserve for Business to $1,000, adds earning cap Chase has just shared two changes that are coming to the Chase Sapphire Reserve for Business℠ (see rates and fees) One change is good news for all cardholders, and the other falls more in the bad news category, but only for a small subset of people. The Edit statement credits increasing to $1,000 per year If you like using the card's two annual statement credits of up to $250 for eligible stays of two nights or longer at The Edit properties booked through Chase Travel℠, you're in luck. Beginning on Jan. 1, 2027, the Chase Sapphire Reserve for Business will offer four statement credits of up to $250 each for The Edit stays that can be used throughout the year. That's up from two statement credits of up to $250 each available on the card in 2026. If fully utilized, this would increase the maximum value of this benefit from $500 to $1,000 each year, $205 more than the card's $795 annual fee. When you stay with Chase's The Edit, you'll receive the following: - Daily breakfast for two - A $100 property credit per booking - A welcome amenity (subject to availability) - Complimentary Wi-Fi at properties that offer Wi-Fi - A room upgrade at check-in (when available) - Early check-in and late checkout (when available) And if you find a lower price for the same eligible The Edit stay within 24 hours of booking through Chase Travel, you may be able to submit a price-match request for the lower rate. Chase did clarify to TPG that this expansion of its The Edit credit benefit only applies to the Chase Sapphire Reserve for Business and not the Chase Sapphire Reserve® (see rates and fees). Chase is adding a $1 million cap to its advertising bonus category One of the unique benefits of the Sapphire Reserve for Business for big-spending businesses has been that its 3-points-per-dollar-spent earning rate for social media and search engine advertising is uncapped. TPG founder Brian Kelly even called this out as something he loved about the card because it was an unusual benefit — most other small-business cards with similar bonus categories have a cap. But the good news is that the limit is very high. Beginning Nov. 15, Chase will cap the 3 points per dollar spent earned on social media and search engine advertising at $1 million in eligible spending per account anniversary year. After that, purchases in those categories will earn 1 point per dollar. For the first year of the new cap, Chase will count eligible spending from Nov. 15, 2026, through the statement on which the cardmember's next annual fee appears. The $1 million cap will then reset each account anniversary year. This cap is much higher than the bonus category spending limits on other similar cards, and Chase says it won't affect the vast majority of cardholders, presumably because most don't spend more than $1 million per year in those categories. Related: Best credit cards for business expenses New cardholders can earn 200,000 bonus points If you want in on the just-announced expanded The Edit credit starting in January, plus all of the Sapphire Reserve for Business's other extensive credits and benefits, the card has a sizable welcome offer: Earn 200,000 bonus Chase Ultimate Rewards points after spending $30,000 on purchases in the first six months from account opening. Based on TPG's September 2026 valuations, that's worth $4,100, which is one of the largest and most valuable welcome bonus offers we've seen from Chase. If your business can comfortably meet the minimum spending requirement, this is a can't-miss offer. Keep in mind approval for the card is subject to Chase's 5/24 rule, which means you won't be approved for this card if you've been approved for five or more personal cards across issuers in the past 24 months. Related: Chase credit cards: Best time to apply based on offer history Bottom line These are the first major changes to the Sapphire Reserve for Business since its debut in 2025. For cardholders who regularly book The Edit stays, doubling the available statement credits to up to $1,000 annually beginning in 2027 could meaningfully increase the card's value. The new advertising cap is a negative change for businesses that spend more than $1 million per account anniversary year on social media and search engine advertising. But with such a high threshold, there's still a lot of room to earn bonus points in those categories. To learn more, read our full review of the Chase Sapphire Reserve for Business.

item.title: Capital One Venture Rewards current offer: 75,000 miles plus a $300 credit for Capital One Travel
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 4.64
Capital One Venture Rewards current offer: 75,000 miles plus a $300 credit for Capital One Travel Editor's Note The Capital One Venture Rewards Credit Card is a great choice for beginners and experienced points-and-miles enthusiasts who want an easy way to earn miles with minimal effort — all for an affordable $95 annual fee. The Venture Rewards card's current welcome offer is especially compelling: Earn 75,000 bonus miles after spending $4,000 on purchases within the first three months from account opening. Plus, you'll receive a $300 credit upon approval to use on hotel and vacation rentals booked through Capital One Travel in the first cardholder year. Here's what the offer is worth and what to know before applying. Capital One Venture Rewards welcome offer New Capital One Venture Rewards cardholders can earn 75,000 bonus miles after spending $4,000 on purchases within the first three months from account opening. Plus, you'll receive a $300 credit upon approval to use on hotel and vacation rentals booked through Capital One Travel in the first cardholder year. Including the credit, this offer is worth $1,688, per TPG's September 2026 valuations. In terms of miles alone, this is the standard welcome bonus on the card. However, the inclusion of the $300 credit makes this offer among the most valuable we've seen. For comparison, previous welcome offers have gone as high as 100,000 miles after meeting the minimum spending requirements (no longer available), but with no credit. It's possible to squeeze even more from that bonus if you redeem Capital One miles for maximum value, thanks to their impressive roster of 15-plus transfer partners. Who is eligible for the Venture Rewards welcome bonus? There are some eligibility requirements to keep in mind before applying. You don't want to waste a hard pull on your credit report if you aren't eligible for the current offer. First, if you've previously earned a welcome bonus on the Venture Rewards, you won't be able to earn another one for 48 months. Note that this is 48 months from the date you received your bonus, not from the date you were approved. In addition, if you previously earned a welcome bonus on the Capital One Venture X Rewards Credit Card, you will more than likely not be eligible to earn a welcome bonus on the Venture Rewards. Capital One may consider multiple factors when deciding whether to approve you; for a deeper dive into its application requirements, check out our full guide. Related: The best Capital One credit cards Earning Capital One miles This card earns at least 2 miles per dollar spent on all purchases. So, by spending $4,000 on it to earn the welcome bonus, you'd earn at least 83,000 miles in the first few months, including the welcome bonus. And since the Venture Rewards earns 5 miles per dollar spent on car rentals, hotels and vacation rentals booked through Capital One Travel, it's possible to earn even more miles while working toward your welcome bonus. While some travel credit cards may earn slightly higher rates on select categories such as groceries or dining, the draw here is the simplicity and guarantee of earning at least 2 miles per dollar spent on anything you buy without the need to memorize multiple bonus spending categories. Related: Why I keep the Capital One Venture Rewards card in my wallet What can Capital One Miles get you? Your total value from this welcome bonus depends largely on how you redeem your miles. There are two key options: - Redeem for 1 cent apiece toward travel - Redeem by transferring to Capital One's 15-plus partner airlines and hotels (our recommendation) When converting your miles to hotel points or airline miles, most partners offer a 1:1 transfer ratio, though a couple of partners have different ratios. You can get great sweet spot redemptions by transferring miles to programs like Air Canada Aeroplan and Air France-KLM Flying Blue. For example, TPG's editor-in-chief, Nick Ewen, transferred 117,000 Capital One miles to Emirates Skywards to upgrade himself and two family members to Emirates first class. This broke down to 39,000 miles per person, a reasonable cost for the upgrade. If you don't want to transfer your miles, you can redeem them by booking a trip through Capital One Travel. These redemptions can be very handy in a world where you may be renting recreational vehicles, booking vacation home rentals or securing a cabin close to home more often than hopping on a flight to the other side of the world. Related: Cashing in Capital One miles? How to get the maximum value when redeeming miles Other Venture Rewards perks The Capital One Venture Rewards doesn't offer the same benefits as more premium travel rewards cards, including its upscale sibling, the Capital One Venture X Rewards. But for its modest $95 annual fee, the Venture Rewards provides some useful benefits: - An up to $120 statement credit for Global Entry or TSA PreCheck application fees - Car rental insurance - Complimentary concierge service - Extended warranty protection - No foreign transaction fees Related: Chase Sapphire Preferred Card vs. Capital One Venture Rewards Bottom line The Capital One Venture Rewards remains a strong option for travelers who value simplicity. It earns at least 2 miles per dollar spent on purchases and gives cardholders access to Capital One's airline and hotel transfer partners, all for a $95 annual fee. Plus, the current welcome offer includes a solid haul of miles and a $300 credit for Capital One Travel, one of the best offers we've seen. Just remember to use your credit in the first cardholder year, or you'll forfeit the value. To learn more, read our full review of the Capital One Venture Rewards card. Learn more: Capital One Venture Rewards Credit Card For Capital One products listed on this page, some of the benefits may be provided by Visa® or Mastercard® and may vary by product. See the respective Guide to Benefits for details, as terms and exclusions apply.

item.title: These are North America's best airports, according to JD Power's 2026 rankings
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 4.62
These are North America's best airports, according to JD Power's 2026 rankings Travelers continue to be fed up with expensive airfare, crowded lounges and full flights, but there's a huge bright spot in the travel experience: the airport. That's according to research from J.D. Power, which released its annual North America airport satisfaction study on Wednesday. The results broadly followed the same trends as last year, with overall satisfaction scores continuing to increase. The study is the latest evidence of a powerful trend that has seen U.S. airports — including those once derided as "third-world" by then-Vice President Joe Biden — undergo drastic transformations into terminals perfectly designed to serve modern passengers, including both frequent flyers and occasional travelers. Related: Washington, DC's Reagan National Airport plans $800 million expansion For the study, J.D. Power divided airports into three categories: "Mega" airports see 33 million or more passengers per year. "Large" airports are transited by 10 million to 32.9 million passengers each year. And "medium" airports serve 4.5 million to 9.9 million passengers annually. The study ranks airports in each category on a scale of 1,000 points. Notably, the average score in each segment was higher than in 2025, which in turn had climbed significantly from 2024. Every category of airport improved even higher than 2025 Customer satisfaction with mega airports was an average of 14 points higher in 2026 compared to the previous year, while large airports gained 13 points and medium airports improved by 16 points. In 2026, Minneapolis-Saint Paul International Airport (MSP) led the mega category, mirroring results from the past two years. The airport scored 684 points. Tampa International Airport (TPA) led large airports with 715 points, and Charleston International Airport (CHS) was the top-performing medium airport with 712 points. In the "mega" category, MSP was followed by Detroit Metropolitan Wayne County Airport (DTW) with 663 points and Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport (PHX) with 642 points. Portland International Airport (PDX) ranked second among large airports with 708 points, while Dallas Love Field (DAL) followed in third place with a score of 698. Ontario International Airport (ONT) in California was the runner-up among medium airports with 705 points, while Indianapolis International Airport (IND) — which has led the category for the last four years — ranked third with a score of 695. You can see the full results at the bottom of this story. Related: New York JFK's $19B rebuild: The giant, new Terminal One is just a year away The results are based on surveys of 24,710 U.S. or Canadian residents who had traveled through at least one U.S. or Canadian airport within the past 30 days. The survey was fielded between July 2025 and July 2026. It focused on seven key factors: - Ease of travel through the airport - Level of trust in the airport - Terminal facilities - Airport staff - Food and retail experience - Experience departing from or arriving at the airport via plane - Experience arriving at or departing from the airport via ground transport What's behind increasing satisfaction with North American airports? The improving experience at North American airports is largely the result of various construction projects completed over the past few years, ranging from brand-new terminal buildings and expansions to runway repairs, which have led to fewer delays. "For the better part of the last decade, nearly every airport, from the largest international hubs to midsized airfields, has undertaken a significant capital improvement project aimed at streamlining passenger flow, adding attractive food and beverage options and improving overall passenger experience," Michael Taylor, J.D. Power's managing director of travel, hospitality and retail, said in a statement. "On the whole, those efforts are finally starting to pay off in the form of higher overall passenger satisfaction scores," Taylor added. "However, when it comes to the individual experiences of passengers, every detail counts and the specific design and structural decisions airports make can have a significant influence on how passengers spend their time — and their money — in the terminal." Related: Chicago O'Hare is a huge construction site — here's what's going up Notably, all of the highest-ranked airports in the study have either recently completed or are nearing completion of extended capital improvement projects, J.D. Power noted. Many of those projects have included major transformations of the food, beverage and retail options in the terminals, giving passengers more options for where to eat or shop before a flight. While many of those improvements have included bringing local color to the airports, finding the right balance with major national chains led to the highest scores, the report found. Or as Taylor put it during the release of last year's report: "A decades-long trend of bringing unique, local flavor to the passenger experience has positively impacted the airport experience with these local touches having a major influence on passenger satisfaction."
