item.title: Amazon Prime members can get $20 off a $30 Grubhub order
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 4.55
Amazon Prime members can get $20 off a $30 Grubhub order Ahead of the Prime Big Deal Days in October, Amazon Prime members can get $20 off a Grubhub+ restaurant order of $30 or more when they use code "DEALS20" at checkout through Oct. 5. This deal is only available to active Grubhub+ members through Amazon Prime when placing a qualifying order on the Grubhub platform, including Seamless, or via the Grubhub digital store available on Amazon. You can only use it once, and your order subtotal must be at least $30 before tax, tip and fees to be eligible. Related: Is the Prime Visa credit card worth the cost? Keep in mind that active Amazon Prime members in the U.S. can link their account to Grubhub and get free access to Grubhub+. Members can also get $10 off their first Grubhub+ restaurant order through Oct. 15 after linking their accounts with code "FIRSTORDER," but the order's subtotal must be at least $20 before tax, tip and fees. As such, if you are an Amazon Prime member and you haven't linked your Prime account to Grubhub yet, consider using the "FIRSTORDER" code on your first order and then the "DEALS20" code on your next order. Just remember that minimum spending requirements and other restrictions, such as the exclusion of orders containing alcohol, apply. And even if you've already linked your accounts, getting $20 off a $30 restaurant order is a substantial discount. Although both codes are valid through October, I wouldn't wait too long to use them, as demand may be high and Grubhub reserves the right to end either or both promotions early. Related reading:

item.title: Elite status, hotel nights and more: Your guide to the Virgin Red Rewards Mastercard
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 4.27
Elite status, hotel nights and more: Your guide to the Virgin Red Rewards Mastercard Editor's Note The Virgin Red Rewards Mastercard®* may have flown under your radar, especially if you don't often fly Virgin Atlantic. But with some useful perks that can easily offset the annual fee, this card is worth a look even for casual Virgin travelers. With a wide range of spending categories that earn bonus rewards, a fast track to status and no foreign transaction fees, this is a card that can be well worth having in your wallet. Read on to learn how to make the most of this card and decide if it's right for you. What is the Virgin Red Rewards Mastercard? The Virgin Red Rewards Mastercard,* issued by Synchrony Bank, is a cobranded card affiliated with Virgin's family of travel programs. It rewards cardholders not only on Virgin Atlantic flights, but also on stays booked through the Virgin Hotels platform and cruises booked through Virgin Voyages. The card technically earns Virgin Points, but these are interchangeable with Virgin Atlantic Flying Club points because your balance shows up in both programs. TPG values Virgin points at 1.45 cents apiece based on our August 2026 estimates, making them one of the more valuable airline currencies on the market. The card carries a $99 annual fee,* but Virgin flyers will find the rewards and benefits more than make up for this. Let's dive in. Related: What's the difference between Virgin Atlantic Flying Club and Virgin Red? Earning points First off, the Virgin Red Rewards Mastercard has a welcome offer of 60,000 bonus points, earned when you spend $4,000 on purchases in the first 90 days from account opening. According to the card page, that's "enough for a reward flight" — but considering that Virgin redemptions start as low as 6,000 points each way, you could potentially book several award flights with a single welcome bonus.* As you might expect, the card earns bonus points on Virgin purchases: 3 points per dollar spent on Virgin Atlantic, Virgin Hotels and Virgin Voyages. It also awards 2 points per dollar spent in several other common categories — grocery stores, dining out, select streaming services and EV charging — and 1 point per dollar spent on all other purchases. That's a solid earning structure, considering many cobranded airline cards offer bonus rewards on purchases with the airline but not on other travel categories. Plus, the elevated earn rate on staples like groceries makes it more rewarding to focus your spending on this card (I'll get into why you may want to do that later). Cardholders also receive 5,000 bonus points on their anniversary each year when they renew the card. That's worth roughly $73 by TPG's valuations, almost enough to offset the card's annual fee. And you can earn 2,500 bonus points each time you add an authorized user (on up to four users). Since there is no fee to add an authorized user, you could maximize this benefit to score 10,000 bonus points (worth $145) right off the bat.* Since you can transfer any of the major credit card currencies to either Virgin Atlantic Flying Club or Virgin Red at a 1:1 ratio, this card could be a perfect complement to another travel rewards credit card of your choice. Plus, all Virgin Atlantic Flying Club members have the ability to pool points with loved ones in a household account, which could make it easier to accrue the points you need for your next trip. Related: Your guide to credit card transfer partners Elite status acceleration Unlike many airline credit cards, the Virgin Red Rewards Mastercard doesn't offer much in the way of day-of-travel benefits like free checked bags and priority boarding. However, the card can help you access these perks if you leverage it to earn Virgin Atlantic Flying Club elite status. You'll earn 25 tier points for every $2,500 of qualifying spend on the card, up to 50 Tier Points per month. That means you could reach Silver status (which requires 400 points in a calendar year) in as little as eight months with spending alone. Or you could get more than halfway to Gold (which requires 1,000 points) if you maximize the tier points on this card over the course of a year.* Tier points are primarily earned by taking Virgin Atlantic flights and spending on the Virgin Red Rewards Mastercard. So, if you want to reap the benefits of elite status but don't fly Virgin often enough to reach it, this card could be a no-brainer. Other perks The card comes with no foreign transaction fees,* an important feature for anyone who travels internationally. Another notable perk is the annual third-night-free benefit: Once a year, cardholders can add a third night for free when booking two nights at participating Virgin Hotels.* These include properties in popular destinations like New York City, New Orleans and London-Shoreditch. Although the list of participating destinations is fairly short, if you travel to one of them, this perk could save you hundreds of dollars, which can help offset the card's annual fee. You can access additional benefits if you hit certain spending thresholds. Cardholders who spend $15,000 on the card in a cardholder year can choose one of six Personal Perks, while those who spend $30,000 in a cardholder year can choose up to two: - Round-trip companion award: Book a companion for no extra points on a Virgin Atlantic flight redemption (taxes and fees apply). - Round-trip cabin upgrade: Upgrade one passenger round-trip on a Virgin Atlantic flight redemption. - Virgin Hotels free night award: Book one free night at a participating Virgin Hotels property in the U.S. or U.K. - Virgin Hotels suite upgrade: Upgrade to a suite at a participating Virgin Hotels property in the U.S. or U.K. - Virgin Voyages bar credit: Save up to $300 on your bar tab on a Virgin Voyages cruise of seven nights or more, or up to $150 on a cruise under seven nights - Virgin Voyages upgrade: Upgrade your sailing to the Blue Extras tier, which includes perks like a Sailing Club cocktail event, $10 daily specialty coffee credit, laundry service and Sailing Club Services Support. These customizable perks can add significant value, and the minimum spend required to earn them should be attainable for many travelers if they put most of their monthly expenses on the card. How to maximize redemptions You can redeem Virgin Points for a wide variety of purchases, including stays through Virgin Hotels, cruises through Virgin Voyages, gym classes through Virgin Active and gift cards at popular brands through Virgin Red. However, you'll generally get the most value from your points when you spend them on reward flights through Virgin Atlantic. According to Virgin's site, "every seat onboard, on any date, can be paid for with Virgin Points."* Award rates can vary widely due to Flying Club's dynamic pricing; you can use tools like Seats.aero or Virgin's Reward Seat Checker to find the best deals. Redemptions are not limited to Virgin-operated flights; you can also redeem points for seat upgrades and partner flights. Virgin has a long list of both SkyTeam and other partner airlines, including Delta, KLM, Air New Zealand and All Nippon Airways (ANA). A few examples of the best ways to maximize your Virgin points include: - Saver fares from the East Coast to London, which start at just 6,000 points each way in economy. - Delta partner fares as low as 7,500 Virgin points each way. - Air France economy tickets to Europe from the West Coast from 15,000 points one-way. - Premium cabin seats to Japan on ANA, which start from 105,000 Virgin points round-trip in business class or 145,000 points roundtrip in a first-class suite seat. Of course, you will still have to pay taxes, fees and surcharges on award tickets. Virgin is known for tacking hefty surcharges onto its own award fares, especially in premium cabins, though partner fares tend to have more reasonable taxes and fees. The Virgin Red Rewards Mastercard could help you maximize your earnings on these charges.* Related: Which Virgin Atlantic Flying Club partner redemptions can be booked online? Bottom line As with many travel rewards cards, the Virgin Red Rewards Mastercard is designed to encourage cardholders to stay within the Virgin ecosystem. You will get the most out of it if you book other travel through Virgin's platforms, or if you fly Virgin Atlantic enough to value Flying Club elite status. However, this card could make a good addition to your wallet even if you're a casual Virgin reward traveler. (And with the program's many transfer partners and low award rates, who isn't?) The card's welcome bonus alone makes it worth considering, and between the yearly third-night-free hotel benefit and 5,000-point anniversary bonus, most travelers should be able to recoup their annual fee. Learn more about the Virgin Red Rewards Mastercard *The Virgin Red Rewards Mastercard® is available to US residents aged 18 or older. Subject to credit approval. Terms apply. Click here for the full terms and to apply for the card. ANNUAL FEE and NO FOREIGN TRANSACTION FEE: New Accounts as of 7/1/26: Variable Purchase APR 19.74%, 23.74% or 27.74%. Variable Bal Trans APR 19.74%, 23.74% or 27.74% and 5% Fee ($5 min). Variable Cash APR 29.74% and 5% Fee ($10 min). Variable Penalty APR 29.74%, 33.74% or 37.74%. Min Interest Charge $2. Annual Fee $99.

item.title: Can you earn a Citi / AAdvantage Executive Mastercard welcome bonus more than once?
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 4.08
Can you earn a Citi / AAdvantage Executive Mastercard welcome bonus more than once? Editor's Note Credit card welcome bonuses are one of the quickest ways to earn valuable travel rewards. You can often pick up 100,000 points or more in a single bonus, which can be worth thousands of dollars in travel. Right now, American Airlines' top-tier card, the Citi® / AAdvantage® Executive World Legend Mastercard® (see rates and fees), is offering new cardholders a best-ever, limited-time bonus to earn 125,000 bonus miles after spending $15,000 on purchases in the first five months from account opening. Based on September 2026 valuations, this offer is worth $1,813. But what if you already have the card or have held it before? Can you earn the welcome bonus on it again? To answer this question, it's important to understand Citi's application rules and identify the exact date when you last earned the welcome bonus on this card. Let me walk you through it. Related: Is the Citi / AA Executive Mastercard worth it? Understanding Citi's application rules On most of its cobranded cards, Citi restricts earning the welcome bonus to once every 48 months. This rule applies to the Citi / AAdvantage Executive. The best way to find out this date is to call Citi at 888-766-2484. Alternatively, you could also call AAdvantage at 800-882-8880. (You can only see your account activity through your AAdvantage online account for the past two years.) Timing is important The 48-month period starts on the date the previous bonus was received, not on the date the account was opened or closed. That's important because a few months will probably have passed between when you were approved for the card and when you met the minimum spending requirement and, thus, received the welcome bonus. Product changes You can earn the welcome bonus on each of Citi's AAdvantage cards once every 48 months — each product is treated separately. In the past three years, I have applied for the following three Citi / AAdvantage cards and earned the welcome bonus on each: However, suppose I had earned the bonus on my Platinum Select and then the product changed (or upgraded) it to the Executive. In that case, I would need to wait 48 months from the date I received the Platinum Select welcome bonus to earn the Executive welcome bonus. The information for the Citi / AAdvantage Platinum Select has been collected independently by The Points Guy. The card details on this page have not been reviewed or provided by the card issuer. Strategies to maximize bonus opportunities Here are some of my top tips for quickly earning a lot of AAdvantage miles by applying for cobranded American Airlines credit cards. Work out your application strategy If you are confident that you received the welcome bonus on your Executive card more than four years ago and don't currently hold the card, you're good to apply for it again. If you currently have the card, first, you'll want to downgrade or cancel it. My recommendation would be to downgrade it to the no-annual-fee American Airlines AAdvantage® MileUp® card by calling Citi at the number on the back of your card. However, note that downgrading will make you ineligible for the MileUp card's (small) welcome bonus. The upside is that you will protect your credit score as there will be no change to your credit report. The information for the AAdvantage MileUp card has been collected independently by The Points Guy. The card details on this page have not been reviewed or provided by the card issuer. Alternatively, you can cancel your Executive card. While this may temporarily hurt your credit score due to an increase in your credit utilization ratio, you may be eligible to earn the welcome bonus on the MileUp should you choose to apply for it in the future. Bottom line Citi's 48-month rule makes timing critical when applying for its AAdvantage credit cards. By tracking when you last earned a welcome bonus and understanding how product changes affect your eligibility, you can ensure you maximize your chances of approval. If you're an AA loyalist sitting on an old bonus, now's the time to reapply — but track that 48-month window carefully or you'll miss out. To learn more about the card, read our full review of the Citi / AAdvantage Executive. item.title: The highest-ever Chase-to-Marriott transfer bonus is back: Get 70% more Marriott Bonvoy points
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 3.75
The highest-ever Chase-to-Marriott transfer bonus is back: Get 70% more Marriott Bonvoy points Good news: The highest Marriott Bonvoy transfer bonus we've ever seen is officially back. From now through Oct. 15, you can get a 70% bonus when transferring Chase Ultimate Rewards points to Marriott Bonvoy. This means if you transferred 100,000 Chase points from cards such as the Chase Sapphire Preferred® Card (see rates and fees) to Marriott, you'd get 170,000 Marriott points instead of the 100,000 points you'd usually get with the normal 1:1 ratio. This is the most generous Marriott transfer bonus we've seen this year, and it ties the highest transfer bonus we've ever seen. Here's how to make the most of this limited-time Chase-to-Marriott transfer bonus and how to decide if it is a good deal for you. Related: Current credit card transfer bonuses Deals available with the 70% Marriott transfer bonus To get you thinking about what is possible, here are a few award stays you could book with this 70% Chase-to-Marriott transfer bonus. Stay within walking distance of Walt Disney World for as low as 36,000 transferred Chase points per night On nights when it is just 60,000 Marriott Bonvoy points per night to stay at the Walt Disney World Swan Reserve, a Marriott hotel that's within walking distance of (or a free boat ride away from) Disney's Hollywood Studios and Epcot, it would cost you just 36,000 transferred Chase points with the 70% bonus. Note that, like at all other Marriott properties, you are still responsible for any resort or destination fees, even when you are staying on points at this and other Marriott properties — we'll circle back to that point shortly. Enjoy an overwater bungalow in Bora Bora from 50,000 transferred Chase points per night Award prices at The Westin Bora Bora Resort & Spa currently start around 84,000 Marriott points per night for a variety of room types, including its iconic overwater bungalows. With the 70% transfer bonus, these bungalows are bookable starting from 50,000 transferred Chase points per night, a solid rate for a stay in absolute paradise. Head to Hawaii for as low as 34,000 transferred Chase points per night You can stay at the fun, colorful Laylow Waikiki, Autograph Collection in Honolulu from just 34,000 transferred Chase points per night, as this 70% transfer bonus will get you the needed 57,000 points to cover a night at the property. If that's not the hotel for you, though, there are plenty of other Marriott properties in the Waikiki area, including the iconic 125-year-old Moana Surfrider, A Westin Resort & Spa, Waikiki Beach, which would also start at 34,000 transferred Chase points per night since it also has some nights that are bookable for 57,000 Marriott points. Have a luxe stay in New York from 63,000 transferred Chase points per night There are plenty of fancy Marriott properties in the Big Apple, but if you want one of the newest and swankiest, you might want to check out The Ritz-Carlton New York, NoMad. For a stay that's more elegant and classic, choose the timeless St. Regis New York. No matter how you slice it, both are pricey hotels, but with the 70% transfer bonus, rooms start at 60,000 transferred Chase points per night at the former and 63,000 transferred Chase points per night at the latter to get you the needed 102,000 and 106,000 points, respectively. Remember, though, that some nights will cost more. How to tell if you should transfer Chase points to Marriott with this bonus Booking a beloved theme park hotel for 36,000 transferred points a night or a bucket list-worthy stay in an overwater bungalow for 50,000 transferred points per night sounds pretty great — and it absolutely can be a tremendous deal. But even with a historically high 70% transfer bonus, moving Chase Ultimate Rewards points to Marriott Bonvoy won't always be your best option. Since point transfers are one way, you'll want to do a little math before hitting that transfer button. TPG currently values Chase points at 2.05 cents each based on our September 2026 valuations because of all the valuable transfer partners you can use them with, while Marriott Bonvoy points are worth 0.75 cents each based on TPG's September 2026 valuations. So, even with a 70% bonus, you are turning 1 Chase point worth 2.05 cents into 1.7 Marriott points worth about 1.3 cents. Average valuations are not the same thing as individual use cases, though. What really matters is how many Chase points — or even how much cash — it will cost to book the specific hotel you want. Before deciding to transfer points, make sure you: - Check the cash rate. You may not want to transfer a large number of valuable Chase points for a hotel that's relatively inexpensive to book with cash. - Check the hotel's price through Chase Travel℠. Depending on the Chase card you have and the hotel you're eyeing, your Chase points may be worth 1 cent each or closer to 2 cents each if the stay is eligible to book via Chase's Points Boost feature. - Check the Marriott award price directly on Marriott's site and divide it by 1.7. That's approximately how many Chase points you'll need to transfer during this 70% bonus. For example, if a hotel costs 60,000 Marriott points, divide 60,000 by 1.7 to get roughly 36,000 transferred Chase points. Then, compare your options. If Marriott wants 60,000 points for a room that would cost 50,000 Chase points through Chase Travel, transferring roughly 36,000 Chase points during this bonus could be the better option. But if Chase Travel only requires 30,000 points for the same room, transferring wouldn't make as much sense. There are a couple of other factors to consider, too. Marriott Bonvoy members get the lowest-priced night free when redeeming points for five consecutive nights, which can make transferring an even better option for longer stays. However, Marriott award stays can still come with resort or destination fees, so be sure to factor them into your comparison. And remember: An elevated transfer bonus like this one can be especially useful if you already have most of the Marriott points required for a specific redemption and just need to top off your account. I wouldn't recommend transferring points to Marriott speculatively without a specific redemption in mind, though, since Marriott award prices fluctuate. Related: 30 of the best Marriott hotels in the world that you can book with points How to earn more Chase points I like to have some of each major loyalty currency available for moments like this when high transfer bonuses come around. If you don't currently have Chase points available, you can be ready for potential future transfer bonuses if you start earning valuable Chase Ultimate Rewards points now via one of these cards: - Chase Sapphire Preferred Card: Earn 75,000 bonus points after spending $5,000 on purchases in the first three months from account opening. - Chase Sapphire Reserve® (see rates and fees): Earn 100,000 bonus points after spending $6,000 on purchases in the first three months from account opening. - Chase Sapphire Reserve for Business℠ (see rates and fees): Earn 200,000 bonus points after spending $30,000 on purchases in the first six months from account opening. Related: Best Chase credit cards Bottom line If you are planning Marriott stays on points, then it absolutely makes sense to run some award searches and see if this limited-time, highest-ever transfer bonus from Chase Ultimate Rewards to Marriott Bonvoy might help you unlock your travel goals. Even though the transfer bonus is the highest we have seen for Marriott, it won't always be the best deal for any specific trip, given how valuable Chase points are. That said, there are absolutely times when the math will be on your side to hit that transfer button, so crunch some numbers to see if you can book the stay you've been dreaming of for fewer points than you thought. Related reading:

A 21+ day advance purchase is required; up to $80 per person in taxes and fees apply. Other restrictions apply. Why we love it: The card offers valuable benefits for frequent Delta flyers, including Delta Sky Club access (subject to eligibility and annual visit limits), Centurion Lounge access, an annual companion certificate and an annual MQD boost. Cardmembers can also receive several statement credits, including up to $200 each calendar year for eligible Delta Stays bookings, up to $240 per calendar year at eligible U.S. Resy restaurants (up to $20 per month) and up to $120 per calendar year with eligible U.S. ride-hailing providers (up to $10 per month). Enrollment is required for select benefits. TPG principal spokesperson Clint Henderson has carried the card for years and values its status benefits and statement credits. "This card has been a workhorse in my wallet for years. I love the status boost, the MQD earning ability, the Resy and ride-hailing credits and the Delta Stays credit. Another perk is that it unlocks a discount on mileage awards, which has come in handy many times for me over the years." To learn more, read our full review of the Delta SkyMiles Reserve. Apply here: Delta SkyMiles Reserve American Express Card Hilton Honors cards Hilton travelers currently have two enticing welcome offers to consider on the Hilton Aspire and Hilton Surpass. Welcome offers: - Hilton Honors Surpass: Earn 130,000 bonus points and a free night reward after spending $3,000 on purchases in the first six months of card membership. - Hilton Honors Aspire: Earn 200,000 bonus points after spending $6,000 on purchases in the first six months of card membership. Why we love them: The Aspire is the premium option, offering automatic Hilton Honors Diamond status and an array of Hilton statement credits and travel perks. The Surpass offers automatic Hilton Honors Gold status and useful Hilton credits with a much lower annual fee, making it a strong choice for more occasional Hilton guests. To learn more, read our full review of the Hilton Honors Aspire and our full review of the Hilton Honors Surpass. Apply here: Hilton Amex Surpass Apply here: Hilton Amex Aspire Bottom line These offers can help you boost your transferable points and miles balance or unlock meaningful discounts on your next trip. As always, be sure to factor in each issuer's unique set of application restrictions and ensure you can meet any spending requirements to earn the bonus. But with so much value on the table, you won't want to miss out on adding one of these top credit cards (and its bonus) to your wallet. item.title: I make my own amenity kit for long flights — here’s what’s inside
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 3.17
I make my own amenity kit for long flights — here’s what’s inside I love a good inflight amenity kit. Seeing a colorful little pouch stocked with travel-size products waiting at my seat is one of my favorite parts of flying in the front of the plane. Airlines often partner with fancy brands familiar to premium flyers, such as Sisley or Kiehl's, to provide skincare goodies in addition to the standard kit-stuffers like earplugs and eye masks. The only thing is, I have a bizarre allergy. While ultra-soothing for most people, aloe vera makes me break out. I know certain brands are safe for me. For example, the Shiseido Men skincare line stocked in Japan Airlines first class and the L'Occitane products in Lufthansa Allegris business class don't make me itch. Unfortunately, many other skincare products contain this scurrilous succulent, so I have to be careful about which amenity kits I use... and which ones I tuck away to take home to my husband. After encountering aloe-laden skincare products in amenity kit after amenity kit (I know, it's like complaining they only pour one type of Champagne in first class), I finally decided to take matters into my own hands. I put together my very own DIY amenity kit for flights so I would know I had all the essentials. And unlike airline amenity kits, I don't have to be flying in a premium cabin in order to enjoy the inclusions. In fact, my little amenity kit comes in even handier on long economy flights since I can primp before I land. Here are the items that I stock my DIY inflight amenity kit with and why I pack each one. Keep in mind, these aren't products like Trtl travel pillows; they are just everyday essentials I like to have on hand. DIY flight amenity kit Short on time? Here's a quick hit list of the things I pack, with links so you can purchase them yourself: Now for the full list. Clear pouch First things first, you need a handy, reusable kit to actually carry everything. Because many of my amenity kit items are liquids and there are TSA rules and all, I tend to pack my kit in a clear pouch like these to save headaches at the airport. In a pinch, I just use a Ziploc bag. Sanitizing wipes I was doing this even before the pandemic. I read article after article about how germy planes are and which surfaces around your seat tend to be dirtiest ... and I just decided to be my own seat cleaner at a certain point. That's why I always carry a pouch of Lysol disinfecting wipes, which will kill just about anything. The only thing to keep in mind is to wash your hands after using them, since you don't want to touch your face with the disinfecting agent. If you don't have an aloe allergy like me, Wet Ones makes skin-friendlier wipes. Hand sanitizer I swear I'm not a germaphobe, but it never hurts to have an extra spurt of sanitizer just in case. Many sanitizing gels also contain aloe, so my go-to is the fancy but inexpensive lavender-scented spray from EO. Tissues You never know when a sneeze will come on ... or if you'll need to pass a tissue to a seatmate, so I always have a travel-size packet of tissues on hand. Toothbrush and toothpaste I don't need these when I'm traveling in business or first class, but if I'm on a long-haul economy flight, I pack an extra-compact folding travel toothbrush. And you'll find a drawer in my bathroom littered with travel-size toothpastes since I go through them at a ridiculous pace. You could consider dry toothpaste tablets to save space (and they won't count against your liquid limit). Earplugs I'm a light sleeper, so even if I'm flying at the pointy end of the plane and receive a kit with soft foam earplugs, I tend to bring my own silicone ones along anyway. I know, I know, the otolaryngologists among you will decry me for waxifying my ears; however, I make sure to clean my ears after flights, and I don't use these too often. The benefit of drowning out cabin noise even outweighs the auricular hazard (for me). If those are too heavy-duty for you, though, you can always switch to the foam pairs. Eye mask From the overheads to the screen of that one person who insists on watching all the episodes of "House of the Dragon" while everyone else is sleeping, there are tons of LED lights in airplane cabins. That's why I always have an eye mask on hand. Even up in business class, where an eye mask might be provided, they tend to be itchy and not breathable, so it never hurts to tote your own. Saline nasal spray One of the worst parts about flying for me is how dried out my nose, mouth and sinuses get. That also makes me prone to catching colds. To solve for that, I always bring a squeezable saline nasal spray. Using a spritz every few hours keeps me breathing comfortably, and I've noticed I get sick a lot less often since I started using it. Lubricating eye drops I try not to overuse this since it can actually make dry eyes worse over time. But my eye doctor said it was perfectly fine to use eye drops on longer flights from time to time and recommended Systane in particular. Chewing gum Like my nose and eyes, my mouth gets dried out on long flights, no matter how much water I drink, so you'll always find a pack of gum in my bag. I tend to chew it during takeoff and landing to help with the pressure changes, too. Hand cream As we have now established, airplane air is dry. That has a big impact on my skin, too, especially my hands (which you now know I've been sanitizing like a fiend). To counteract all that, I make sure to have Cerave hand lotion with me. I find it moisturizes super well, and even a small tube lasts me several months. Facial wipes I can't imagine much that's grosser than washing your face with airplane lavatory water. Except drinking it, I suppose. Don't do either. Instead, after an inflight snooze, use some gentle face wipes to freshen up before using the next DIY amenity kit inclusion. Face lotion I like to step off the plane glowing. Kidding. I just want to look like a human being and not a zombie. So I make sure to have some heavy-duty face cream with me. Cerave's inexpensive eye repair cream does the trick — it's great for the sensitive area under your eyes, and you also only need a small amount for the rest of your face. It's also unscented, so no one will know your secret to looking so fresh. If you really want to plump up your skin with that glowing, dewy look (and you lack the self-consciousness gene), you could always apply Summer Fridays jet lag hydrating eye patches, too. Lip balm Go as fancy or as frugal as you like. I'm a simple guy, so my lip balm of choice is Chapstick with SPF. I can apply it on the plane and know my skin will be well-protected even if I land in the middle of the day. Deodorant You've dashed to the airport on public transport or via Uber. You've hauled your checked bag to the desk, parkoured around oblivious travelers shuffling aimlessly through the airport terminal and then settled into a seat that's always too hot or too cold but never just right. You're going to need some deodorant after a long flight, so pack a small stick to use in a pinch. A pen I'm that guy. You know, the one who seems to be the only responsible adult on the plane with an actual pen. I'm the guy everyone else is asking to borrow his pen to fill out immigration and customs forms, or just to make a note on something. So you be that guy, too. It'll save me from losing all the pens I have to loan out! A pill pack Especially on the long-haul flights I'm used to taking, which can last up to 16 hours, I like to keep a stock of my daily vitamins and supplements, plus a few Ibuprofen and Tylenol just in case. I don't want to pack tons of pill bottles, though. Instead, I bring a travel pill pack with various compartments so I can bring what I need for the flight and leave the rest in my checked or carry-on bag.

item.title: 9 great ways to use Bilt Cash — from bonus points to helicopter rides
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 2.82
9 great ways to use Bilt Cash — from bonus points to helicopter rides Editor's Note When the revamped Bilt program launched in early 2026, one of the biggest additions was Bilt Cash. Only $100 of Bilt Cash rolls forward per calendar year, with the rest expiring on Dec. 31. That means you don't want to let it sit for too long. With Bilt, you can earn both redeemable Bilt Points and Bilt Cash. And with the Bilt credit cards, you can earn both types of rewards at the very same time. Most of us are probably at least somewhat familiar with how to use traditional points, but Bilt Cash is a newer part of the program with a growing list of redemption options. If you've been racking up 4% in Bilt Cash on every dollar charged to a Bilt credit card and planning to figure out how to use it "one day," let me encourage you to make that day now. The good news is that there are now lots of great ways to use it, so here are some of our favorite ways to use Bilt Cash here at TPG, starting with the options that can potentially stretch it the furthest. How to earn Bilt Cash First, a quick overview of how you earn Bilt Cash. You earn some Bilt Cash when you reach certain milestones within Bilt, such as for every 25,000 Bilt points you earn toward your status. If you choose to earn Bilt Cash instead of housing-only rewards, you'll earn 4% in Bilt Cash on eligible nonhousing purchases with the three Bilt credit cards. New cardholders can also receive a chunk of Bilt Cash upon approval, depending on the card: - Bilt Blue Card (see rates and fees): Receive $100 in Bilt Cash when you apply and are approved and can earn 4% in Bilt Cash on non-housing purchases on the card. - Bilt Obsidian Card (see rates and fees): Receive $200 in Bilt Cash when you apply and are approved, plus you can earn 4% in Bilt Cash on non-housing purchases. - Bilt Palladium Card (see rates and fees): Earn 50,000 bonus points and Bilt Gold status (through the rest of the calendar year in which it was earned and the following calendar year) after spending $4,000 on everyday purchases in the first 90 days from account opening. Additionally, cardholders receive $300 in Bilt Cash upon approval and can earn 4% in Bilt Cash on non-housing purchases on the card. Related: TPG Bilt calculator helps you choose how to earn the most rewards with Bilt Best ways to use Bilt Cash There isn't one universally best redemption, but some options can earn more Bilt points or more value than others. Earn Bilt points on your rent or mortgage payment One of the ways to redeem Bilt Cash is to cash it in to earn transaction-fee-free points while paying your rent or mortgage via Bilt. This costs $30 in Bilt Cash for every $1,000 in housing payments that you want to earn points on via Bilt. For example, if your monthly housing payment is $3,000, it would cost you $90 in Bilt Cash to earn 1 point per dollar on that full amount for a total of 3,000 points. There is a setting in Bilt to automatically use your Bilt Cash this way each month. From a pure points-earning perspective, this is one of the stronger standing uses of Bilt Cash. And Bilt members appear to agree. Bilt told TPG that unlocking points on rent and mortgage payments accounts for a significant portion of Bilt Cash usage. Beyond housing, the company said members have also shown strong engagement with local restaurants and fitness studios. If you want to earn points on your housing payment but don't earn enough Bilt Cash to fully utilize both this option and the Points Accelerator, know that the housing option is mathematically a bit more generous. So, I'd recommend prioritizing earning points on your housing payment if you have to choose between the two. Use Bilt Cash to unlock better transfer bonuses Sometimes, on the first of the month, during what Bilt calls 'Rent Day,' there are transfer bonuses to one of Bilt's hotel or airline partners, with those with higher Bilt elite status often receiving larger bonuses. In some cases, you can use Bilt Cash to "buy up" one status level and unlock a larger transfer bonus. For example, on a recent Rent Day, Bilt Gold members received a 45% transfer bonus to Virgin Red. But those same Gold members could spend $200 in Bilt Cash to upgrade to the Bilt Platinum bonus tier, which offered a 75% transfer bonus. If you were transferring 100,000 Bilt points to Virgin Red, spending that $200 in Bilt Cash would get you an additional 30,000 Virgin points compared with the standard Gold transfer bonus. That's a fantastic return on $200 in Bilt Cash — and, in that specific example, far better mathematically than using the same amount of Bilt Cash for the Points Accelerator or even earning points on your housing payment. Earn more points with the Points Accelerator Whether you pay your housing via Bilt or not, one valuable use of Bilt Cash is to earn an extra point per dollar on everyday purchases with the Bilt Obsidian Card or Bilt Palladium Card via what Bilt calls its Points Accelerator. This option isn't available with the Bilt Blue Card. For $200 in Bilt Cash, you can activate the Points Accelerator in your Bilt app to earn an extra point per dollar on the next $5,000 in non-housing purchases on your Obsidian or Palladium Card through the end of the year. You can do this up to five times per calendar year. When this Points Accelerator option is activated, these cards earn: - Obsidian: 4 points per dollar spent on grocery (up to $25,000 spent each year, then 1 point per dollar) or dining, 3 points per dollar spent on travel, 2 points per dollar on everyday spend - Palladium: 3 points per dollar spent on non-housing everyday spending You need to manually go into your Bilt account and activate the Points Accelerator option each time — there's no setting that auto-renews it when the $5,000 is fully utilized, though there is a tracker to show your progress toward spending the full $5,000. Max out the full $5,000 in spending, and your $200 in Bilt Cash will have earned you an additional 5,000 Bilt points. Put another way, the Points Accelerator costs $40 in Bilt Cash per 1,000 additional points, compared with $30 per 1,000 points when using Bilt Cash toward housing. That's why I'd generally prioritize housing first if you have to choose between the two. That said, being able to turn the Palladium Card into a 3-points-per-dollar-on-virtually-everything card with the click of a button and $200 in Bilt Cash is absolutely phenomenal, if you ask me. Related: My Bilt Palladium mid-year update: What's changed since January Use Bilt Cash toward hotel stays Another popular use of Bilt Cash is toward hotel stays booked through Bilt Travel. You can redeem up to $100 in Bilt Cash (depending on your elite status tier) toward hotel stays of two nights or longer booked through Bilt Travel, up to once per calendar month. What's really cool about this option is that you can stack it with the Bilt Palladium Card's up to $400 in annual hotel credits, for hotel bookings made through the Bilt Travel portal (up to $200 biannual statement credits from January through June and July through December). You must book a minimum stay of two nights. Stacked together, you can essentially save up to $300 on two two-night hotel stays per year using Bilt Cash and the Palladium Card's credits. That's exactly how I saved $300 on a stay at The Villas at Disneyland Hotel that I booked via Bilt earlier this year. Other ways to use Bilt Cash Not every Bilt Cash redemption needs to maximize your theoretical return. If you have a balance to use before Dec. 31, several lifestyle options can provide straightforward savings. Use Bilt Cash on Blade helicopter rides A newer way to use Bilt Cash is on up to two Blade helicopter seats per calendar year, at a rate of up to $350 in Bilt Cash per seat. Blade operates between Manhattan and both John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK) and Newark Liberty International Airport (EWR), as well as to some farther-afield spots such as the Hamptons, making this a pretty fun way to spend down a bunch of Bilt Cash in a hurry. Use Bilt Cash on Blacklane car service Another newer way to use Bilt Cash is on Blacklane car service. If you aren't familiar, Blacklane is a service with professional chauffeurs in high-end cars. You can redeem up to $150 in Bilt Cash per year toward Blacklane in one transaction, with the exact amount tied to your Bilt elite status level. - Up to $150 annually for Bilt Platinum members - Up to $100 annually for Bilt Gold members - Up to $50 annually for Bilt Blue and Silver members Use Bilt Cash to pay for fitness classes You can redeem up to $40 a month in Bilt Cash toward workout classes bookable via Bilt. Some big-name fitness options include Barry's and SoulCycle, but there are more local options available, too. One bonus perk of booking with a Bilt partner such as Barry's is that you also get a smoothie from the Barry's Fuel Bar after class when you book your workout through the Bilt app. Use Bilt Cash on Lyft If you regularly use Lyft to get around, an easy money-saving use of Bilt Cash is to redeem $10 per month for Lyft ride credits. TPG Tip: You can also earn 2 Bilt points per dollar when using Lyft, even if you aren't paying with a Bilt credit card, as long as you have linked your Lyft and Bilt accounts and have the card you use to pay for your Lyft rides in your Bilt wallet. To link your Bilt and Lyft accounts, open your Bilt account and navigate to the Neighborhood Benefits section. Once there, select "Rideshare" and follow the prompts. After you link your Bilt and Lyft accounts, open the Lyft app and ensure Bilt is selected as your preferred travel partner. Use Bilt Cash at Walgreens A final popular use of Bilt Cash for some in the TPG offices is at Walgreens, where you can use $10 of Bilt Cash each month toward Walgreens purchases. When you redeem $10 in Bilt Cash, you'll get a $10 Walgreens gift card that's stored in the gift card tab of your Bilt app. You can then use it in-store or online for Walgreens purchases. Bottom line As the year has gone by, Bilt Cash has only gotten better and better as more uses have been introduced. Personally, I use my Bilt Cash first to earn points on my mortgage each and every month, and I'm now on my fourth Points Accelerator option for the year so that I earn 3 points per dollar on everyday spending on my Bilt Palladium Card. I've also used $100 in Bilt Cash twice this year towards hotel stays booked via Bilt Travel — both times in connection with using one of the biannual $200 hotel credits (total of $400 each year) that come with my Bilt Palladium Card. I've made a few smaller Bilt Cash redemptions, too, such as using it for Lyft rides when I'm in New York City. Now I'm running a little low on Bilt Cash, so I probably won't have much trouble using the rest before Dec. 31, when all but $100 of my balance will expire. Luckily, the clock starts all over again on Jan. 1. As a Palladium cardholder, I'll get another $200 in Bilt Cash beginning on January 1, and all those annual redemption limits will reset for another year. To learn more, check out our reviews for the Bilt Palladium, Bilt Obsidian and Bilt Blue cards. Apply here: Bilt Palladium Card Apply here: Bilt Obsidian Card Apply here: Bilt Blue Card
